# swarmops op undo

Move every ref operation OP moved back to what it named before, all or none.

Each ref must still name what the operation set it to (or what it named before, which is skipped): one that was moved since stops the undo with E\_CAS\_MISMATCH, and nothing is written. An undo run again is a replay (already\_applied). Changesets are never removed.

```yaml
title: "swarmops op undo"
description: "Move every ref operation OP moved back to what it named before, all or none."
group: "operations"
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
mcp_tool: "undo"
envelope_op: "undo"
exit_codes: [0, 1, 6]
errors: [E_NOTHING_TO_UNDO, E_OP_NOT_FOUND]
syntax: "swarmops op undo [OPTIONS] <OP>"
```

## Syntax

```text
swarmops op undo [OPTIONS] <OP>
```

## Required arguments

### `OP`

Syntax: `<OP>`.

The operation, as op log numbers it.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

## Examples

### CLI

```sh
swarmops --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17 op undo 0
```

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "op": "undo",
  "api": 1,
  "error": {
    "code": "E_NOTHING_TO_UNDO",
    "message": "operation 0 moved no ref, so there is nothing to undo",
    "retryable": false,
    "exit": 1,
    "details": {
      "op": 0
    },
    "hint": "swarmops op log"
  },
  "meta": {
    "repo": "[tmp]/store",
    "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
    "resolved": {},
    "auth": "trust"
  }
}
```

Exit code 1. Recorded by the CLI tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time.

### MCP

No recorded example yet.

## Return information

`result` is a `UndoResp` (`swarmops schema UndoResp` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `already_applied` | `boolean` | yes | Every ref the operation moved already names what it named before, so nothing was written: an undo run again is a replay, and safe. |
| `op` | `integer or null` | no | The operation this undo recorded, which another undo can take; omitted when it wrote nothing (`already_applied`). |
| `ref_moves` | `array of RefMoveOut` | yes | The moves it made: each ref from what the operation set back to what it named before. |
| `undone` | `integer` | yes | The operation undone. |
| `warnings` | `array of string` | no | Problems found after the undo became durable, such as failed housekeeping; the undo itself succeeded. Omitted when empty. |

Envelope `op`: `undo`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
- `1`: The operation failed.
- `6`: Something the request names does not exist.

## Errors

- [`E_NOTHING_TO_UNDO`](../errors.md#e_nothing_to_undo) (exit 1): The operation moved no ref, so there is nothing to restore.
- [`E_OP_NOT_FOUND`](../errors.md#e_op_not_found) (exit 6): The store has no operation by that number.

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
